insight: During the match between the United States and Bosnia-Herzegovina, the hydration breaks had distinct effects on each team's attacking momentum. At the first break, the United States' attacking actions decreased slightly, with a drop of 0.20 actions per minute, indicating a minor loss of momentum, while Bosnia-Herzegovina's remained unchanged. In contrast, at the second break, the United States slightly increased their attacking actions, whereas Bosnia-Herzegovina also increased theirs, but to a similar extent, suggesting that neither team gained a significant advantage from the breaks, although Bosnia-Herzegovina may have benefited slightly more overall due to their increased attacking actions in the later stages of the match. Overall, the hydration breaks seemed to have a relatively neutral impact on the match, with neither team able to capitalize on them to gain a substantial advantage.
